claim: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (JFE 2018) find, on SPY over 1993–2013, that the first half-hour return measured from the previous close predicts the last half-hour return. In the working-paper version, timing the last half-hour on that signal earned 6.3% a year gross against −0.5% for always holding it, with frictions ignored.

evidence.quote: the first half-hour return on the market as measured from the previous day’s market close predicts the last half-hour return.

Holding SPY (cash) during the last half-hour when the first half-hour return is positive (negative) generates a gross annualized return of 6.3%, compared to -0.5% for holding SPY during all last half-hours.

claim: Later checks are weak: on SPY from Aug 2012 to May 2014 the first/last half-hour correlation was 0.12 (R² 0.014), and Rosa (JFM 2022) finds that the overnight-return variant's predictability disappears out of sample.

evidence.quote: The Pearson correlation for the relationship is 0.12 and the R-squared statistic 0.014, indicating that first half-hour return explains 1% to 2% of the variation in last half-hour return.
The predictability disappears in the out‐of‐sample period.

claim: Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (JFE 2021) find market intraday momentum across more than 60 futures, from 1974 to 2020, and link it to gamma-hedging demand.

evidence.quote: we find strong market intraday momentum everywhere.

claim: A self-published ORB working paper reports a Sharpe ratio of 2.81 and 36% annual alpha for the top-20 stocks in play over 2016–2023. Its QQQ version (33.2% vs 14.9% CAGR) assumed zero slippage. An independent 2015–2026 replication on index CFDs found at most +0.06R out of sample over 2021–2026.

evidence.quote: A portfolio that consisted of the top 20 Stocks in Play achieved a total net performance of over 1,600%, with a Sharpe ratio of 2.81, and an annualized alpha of 36%.

A 5-minute opening range breakout day-trading strategy on QQQ (long/short after first 5 minutes; 1% risk per trade; daily exit) outperformed buy-and-hold QQQ (33.2% vs 14.9% CAGR; Jan 2016–Feb 2023; 1,795 trades; zero slippage assumed).
The out-of-sample years 2021 to 2026 give +0.06 R on NQ at best; futures with commission only were not tested.

claim: Lou, Polk & Skouras (JFE 2019) find that momentum and reversal profits are earned either entirely overnight or entirely intraday, typically with opposite signs across the two.

evidence.quote: profits are either earned entirely overnight (for reversal and a variety of momentum strategies) or entirely intraday, typically with profits of opposite signs across these components.
